questions.q: On the Contact object, what does the AccountId field store?
options: The Id of the Account the contact belongs to, as a lookup relationship
The contact's own record Id
The account's billing address
The account's name as plain text
questions.explain: AccountId is a lookup field holding the Id of the related Account. Relationship queries in Chapter 3 follow this stored Id.

questions.q: Why is WHERE IsClosed = false a safer way to find open Cases than listing every open Status value?
options: IsClosed is maintained by Salesforce from the Status, while each org defines its own status values
IsClosed = false runs faster because it skips the Case table
Status values are identical in every org, so listing them is redundant
Status cannot be used in a WHERE clause
questions.explain: Each org customizes its status picklist, so a hard-coded list can miss values. IsClosed is derived by Salesforce from the status.

questions.q: How do you write a filter for Contacts that have an Email value in SOQL?
options: WHERE Email = ''
WHERE HAS(Email)
WHERE Email != null
WHERE Email IS NOT NULL
questions.explain: SOQL tests for a populated field with != null, the equivalent of IS NOT NULL in T-SQL.

questions.q: In a SOQL WHERE clause, how should you write the boolean and currency values in IsClosed = false and AnnualRevenue > 1000000?
options: The boolean in quotes and the currency with a dollar sign
Both wrapped in single quotes
Both as bare literals with no quotes, and no currency symbol
Booleans must be written as 0 and 1
questions.explain: Booleans are written true or false and numbers are bare values. Only string values, such as picklist values, go in single quotes.

questions.q: Where can you confirm a field's exact API name and data type before writing a query?
options: Only by asking a Salesforce administrator to run the query
By running SELECT * on the object
The label shown on the record's page layout, which is always identical
Setup, Object Manager, then the object's Fields & Relationships list
questions.explain: Object Manager lists each field's API name and type. Page-layout labels can differ, and SELECT * does not exist in SOQL.
